et koma.explanation: "Et koma" means "a coma". To say someone is in a coma, use "i koma" (in a coma): "Hun lå i koma i to uger" (She was in a coma for two weeks). Spell it with one "m".

et komfur.explanation: "Et komfur" means "a stove". To say where a pot sits, use "på komfuret" (on the stove): "Suppen står på komfuret" (The soup is on the stove).

et komma.explanation: "Et komma" means "a comma". In numbers, Danish uses a comma where English uses a point: "tre komma fem" (three point five), written "3,5". Spell it with two "m".

et kommunalvalg.explanation: "Et kommunalvalg" means "a local election". It is built from "en kommune" (a municipality) and "et valg" (an election). To say you vote in it, use "at stemme" (to vote) with "ved": "Jeg stemmer ved kommunalvalget" (I vote in the local election).

et kompagni.explanation: "Et kompagni" means "a company (military or business)". As a business, it appears in the name "Det Østasiatiske Kompagni" (the East Asiatic Company).

et kompas.explanation: "Et kompas" means "a compass". For a person's sense of right and wrong, use "et moralsk kompas" (a moral compass): "Hun har et stærkt moralsk kompas" (She has a strong moral compass).

et kompliment.explanation: "Et kompliment" means "a compliment". To answer a compliment, say "Tak for komplimentet" (Thanks for the compliment).

et kompromis.explanation: "Et kompromis" means "a compromise". To say people reach one, use "at indgå et kompromis" (to reach a compromise): "De indgik et kompromis" (They reached a compromise).

et koncerthus.explanation: "Et koncerthus" means "a concert hall". It is built from "en koncert" (a concert) and "et hus" (a house). One in Copenhagen is called "DR Koncerthuset".

et konditori.explanation: "Et konditori" means "a pastry shop / café". It comes from "en konditor" (a pastry chef).

et kondom.explanation: "Et kondom" means "a condom". To say you use one, Danish leaves out "et": "at bruge kondom" (to use a condom).

et kongehus.explanation: "Et kongehus" means "a royal family". It is built from "en konge" (a king) and "et hus" (a house), so it is literally a "king house".

et kongerige.explanation: "Et kongerige" means "a kingdom". It is built from "en konge" (a king) and "et rige" (a realm). Denmark's official name is "Kongeriget Danmark" (the Kingdom of Denmark), which also includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

et kongresmedlem.explanation: "Et kongresmedlem" means "a member of Congress". It is built from "kongres" (congress) and "et medlem" (a member). For a member of the Danish parliament, use "et folketingsmedlem": "Hun er folketingsmedlem" (She is a member of the Danish parliament).

et konsulat.explanation: "Et konsulat" means "a consulate". It comes from "en konsul" (a consul). To say where you are going, use "på konsulatet" (at the consulate): "Jeg skal på konsulatet i morgen" (I am going to the consulate tomorrow).

et kontantbeløb.explanation: "Et kontantbeløb" means "a cash amount". It is built from "kontant" (in cash) and "et beløb" (an amount). To say you pay in cash, use "kontant": "Jeg betaler kontant" (I pay in cash).

et kontinent.explanation: "Et kontinent" means "a continent". Some continent names are spelled differently from English: "Europa" (Europe) and "Asien" (Asia).

et kontor.explanation: "Et kontor" means "an office". To say where you are, use "på kontoret" (at the office): "Jeg er på kontoret" (I am at the office).

et kontorhus.explanation: "Et kontorhus" means "an office building". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "et hus" (a house).

et kor.explanation: "Et kor" means "a choir". To say people do something all together, use "i kor" (in chorus): "De råbte i kor" (They shouted in chorus).

et kors.explanation: "Et kors" means "a cross". For the X you tick on a form, use "et kryds" (an X mark): "Sæt et kryds her" (Put an X here).

et kort.explanation: "Et kort" means "a map or a card". When you mean a map, say "et kort over Danmark" (a map of Denmark). When you mean a card, say "et kreditkort" (a credit card). The same spelling is also the adjective "short": "en kort tur" (a short trip).

et kortspil.explanation: "Et kortspil" means "a card game". It is built from "et kort" (a card) and "et spil" (a game). To say you play cards, use "at spille kort" (to play cards): "Vi spiller kort i aften" (We are playing cards tonight).

et kosttilskud.explanation: "Et kosttilskud" means "a dietary supplement". It is built from "kost" (diet) and "et tilskud" (an addition).

et kostume.explanation: "Et kostume" means "a costume". To name a party where everyone dresses up, use "en kostumefest" (a costume party): "Vi holder kostumefest" (We are having a costume party).
